newsitem.title: UK: Russian tax regime stunts gas investment - minister.
newsitem.headline: Russian tax regime stunts gas investment - minister.

text.p: Russia's uncompetitive tax structure is hampering investment in the country's gas industry, Pyotr Rodionov, minister of fuel and energy of the Russian federation, said on Monday.

Rodionov told an industry conference that "investors are ready to invest in China and Vietnam but not Russia. Why? Taxes are between 45 percent and 75 percent, twice what they are in the U.S. and Canada and electricity prices for industry are much higher than elsewhere".
"The British had the right approach," Rodionov added. "First they invented football, then they wrote the rules, then they started to play.
"In Russia we started playing, then started thinking about what we were playing and only then started to write the rules".

He added that despite press sepculation on breaking up Gasprom, the Russian gas giant, the company will remain a monopoly and aim to be run as efficiently as possible. "Gasprom will not be breaking up," he said.
